messages:
lina: anyone run into redwoodctl losing auth when running `redwoodctl local serve` inside a Docker dev image on WSL2? starts fine then 401s after a few requests.

omar: i saw this yesterday. are you bind-mounting ~/.redwood? how is the image user configured?

lina: yeah: -v ~/.redwood:/home/dev/.redwood:ro because i don't want containers writing to my host cache. container runs as uid 1000, host files are uid 1001.

lina: error looks like:

lina: ```
ERROR auth: cache write failed: permission denied
request: unauthorized (401)
```

tess: read-only mount + uid mismatch explains it. redwoodctl will try to refresh and persist a token; if it can't write the cache the process keeps using the stale token until TTL expires and then falls back to anonymous.

omar: two practical fixes: (1) start container with REDWOOD_TOKEN env var for short jobs, (2) run the host auth proxy and set REDWOOD_AUTH_URL so the container asks host for fresh tokens instead of writing files.

raul: note: older redwoodctl versions poll the cache file; newer ones use inotify/filewatch and a small background refresher service. mismatched versions between host and image cause subtle races.

lina: ugh. we have prebaked images pinned to v0.12. If host is v0.13 the filewatcher writes updates host-side that the old binary doesn't detect.

omar: workaround without rebuilding images: mount the cache read-only but inject a short-lived token env var into the container via CI/job runner. example:

omar: ```bash
docker run -e REDWOOD_PROFILE=dev \
  -e REDWOOD_TOKEN="$(cat ~/.redwood/cache/dev/token)" \
  -v ~/.redwood:/home/dev/.redwood:ro my-dev-image
```

raul: longer term: we should add a `--container-mode` toggle to redwoodctl so it avoids filewatch reliance and does non-interactive refresh via auth endpoint. also: emit a clear warning when cache writes fail and exit nonzero for CI to catch it. filing followup.

devex-bot: Created DE-2569: "redwoodctl: container-mode flag, cache-perm diagnostics, and non-interactive auth refresh"

tess: also added a short troubleshooting snippet to the localserve docs: cover uid/gid mismatches, ro vs rw mounts, binary parity, and quick env-token injection for ephemeral runs.

lina: thanks — the env-token trick saved our test jobs. i'll watch DE-2569 for updates. :thumbsup:
